A Gluttonous Paradise
Dec 2018 • Couples
Been to two Kichi-Kichi places in Danang -- the one in Lotte Mart and the one on the dragon bridge street -- and can definitely recommend. Like the other reviews say, get there early. When it gets crowded you may have to wait a bit for the popular items like meat and fish. And whatever you do, don't sit directly in front of a fatty, as they will take all the good stuff before it gets to you on the conveyor belt. If you're patient and persistent, however, you'll leave with an over-full belly and a contentment that can only be described as stuffed-to-the-gills. It's like $10 or so which isn't too bad. Plus, if you sneak some meat and veggies into your pockets or purse you'll have enough food for the following day as well! I'm on the Ketogenic diet and there was definitely enough there that was conducive to this eating style FYI.

The restaurant is a hot pot buffet with an extra option for sushi. They had us choose the broth first and there were 2 non spicy choices...so they said. It was still spicy. Also didn’t have a pleasant flavor.

Although we arrived at a busy time, the only food on the belt were noodles and the same vegetables on repeat. It was very boring.

Bathroom had 2 toilets, one without a seat and the other had a broken hinge and didn’t fit the toilet. No hand soap or hand towels.
For four people our bill was $43 and we got food elsewhere after leaving. The entire time we were in Da Nang we were paying almost nothing for meals so this was a horrible mistake coming here.

Lunch at the Zoo
Mar 2017 • Family
We arrived right on lunch time, and the restaurant was packed. After giving our name to the waitress we waited for about 30 minutes to get a seat. Once allocated, we were straight into it. The waitress was efficient, and we ordered 3 hotpots - mushroom (for the kids), Tom Yum (for the wife), and Spicy (for myself).
And then the feast began. The "rotary" delivery of food is typical Japanese fast food style - a large conveyor belt runs around the restaurant (which must hold around 150 people), and takes about 4 minutes to do a circuit. Food is a combination of meat (beef and pork), seafood (fish, octopus, squid), and veges (mainly greens, but also some corn cobs, and various others). Loving my beef, over 1 1/2 hours I must have consumed around 1 kilo of meat. The waitress kept relieving me, and all the other patrons, of our stacked, empty plates, and the food just kept coming (as you would expect from a conveyor belt!). My guests also ate heartily. We were all well satiated when our time to leave arrived.
Now about the Zoo part. While waiting for a seat, all there was to do was to look at the patrons gorging themselves. Once seated, it was difficult to have a conversation, as you sat next to each other, as opposed to opposite, so all there was to do was eat, and look at the patrons waiting to be fed! Also, patrons reached across the conveyor to select the "best" dishes, oblivious to a continuous flow of food. This resulted in quite a lot of spillage. And the waiters had to push their way through to collect the plates. 
In summary, could not complain about the quality or quantity of the food, and the price was very good. However, the total dining experience was like a visit to the Zoo at feeding time.
